conviction_note: The priced bar is the company's own 17-Jun guide of Q1 FY27 revenue +15-20% y/y and GM +1-2pts, set when only May adjusted-NICS (+3.2%) was published; June (+11.7%) and July (+8.5%) both landed afterwards and take the quarter-aligned industry number to +7.7%, and two independent coincident reads (Ruger's Apr-Jun print, Sportsman's Warehouse's quarter ended 1-Aug reported two days ago) point the same way, so I lean to a revenue beat on a stock de-rated 16% in 20 days with only two covering analysts and no company news I can find to explain it; I hold the number to about a third of the 13.2% implied move because findings 1-4 are one correlated thesis and the bear case (Q4's +26.7% having been tariff pull-forward, a seasonally loss-making Q1, +$20m incremental capex) is live.

findings.finding: SWBI's Q1 FY27 guide of +15-20% revenue was given 2026-06-17 with only May adjusted NICS (+3.2% y/y) published; June came in +11.7% (1,123,006 vs 1,004,986) and July +8.5% (1,061,883 vs 978,731), so the two months the guide could not see were 3-4x stronger than the one it could, and the quarter-aligned May-July industry number is +7.7% y/y (3,290,647 vs 3,055,402).
findings.why_not_priced: Each month is published separately and gets a one-day headline; nobody publishes the sum aligned to SWBI's 30-April fiscal year, so the number that matters for this print does not exist anywhere in the wire. If the market had done this arithmetic, the two analysts carrying FY27 estimates would have moved them: stockanalysis.com still shows FY27 revenue consensus of $550.96m, only +5.18% on FY26's $523.85m, against a company that just printed +26.7% in Q4 and guided Q1 to +15-20%, with price targets last updated 2026-07-17 and unchanged through the June and July data. A de-rating of 16.4% over 20 days into a print whose industry backdrop improved is the opposite of what the tape would look like if this were priced.
findings.independence: Sturm Ruger's 8-K for the coincident Apr-Jun quarter says sell-through rose 19% 'exceeding a 5% increase in adjusted NICS' and that distributors' inventories fell 45,800 units - a second manufacturer confirming the industry re-accelerated in the same window (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000095029/000117494726000725/ex99-1.htm). NOTE: this finding shares the Outdoor Wire NSSF releases with finding 2; collapse those two to one source cluster.

findings.finding: NFA (suppressor/SBR) background checks are exploding after the 1-Jan-2026 elimination of the $200 tax stamp - June 2026 166,677 (+177.1% y/y) and July 2026 130,013 (+108.8%) - and SWBI's own Reg FD Investor Day deck filed 2026-07-15 discloses suppressor revenue +95.6% in the first six months of calendar 2026 against a US category it sizes at $700-950m; the June/July NFA data postdates the window that 95.6% covers, so the current run rate is higher than the only figure the company has published.
findings.why_not_priced: Gemtech is not a reported segment and carries no line in any published SWBI model - the FY27 consensus of +5.18% revenue growth cannot contain a doubling business, and the deck was filed as a 7.01 Reg FD 8-K rather than press-released, picking up only StockTitan and one retail blog. If this were priced, the two analysts would have a suppressor line and a target above $12.31, not a $17.25 average set on 2026-07-17 that the stock ignores. It is also a gross-margin item, not just revenue, which is the specific thing the company guided up 1-2pts.
findings.independence: Independent government series confirming the category inflection: FBI/NSSF NFA checks +108.8% y/y in July 2026 (https://www.theoutdoorwire.com/releases/2026/08/nssf-adjusted-nics-background-checks-for-july-2026/). Caveat stated plainly: the NFA numbers come from the same Outdoor Wire releases used in finding 1, so the genuinely separate document here is the SWBI 8-K exhibit.

findings.finding: Sportsman's Warehouse reported its quarter ended 2026-08-01 on 2026-09-01 - two days before SWBI prints and covering almost exactly SWBI's May-July fiscal Q1 - with hunting and shooting sports same-store sales +6.7%, and CEO Paul Stone saying on the call 'Firearms up 8% and ammo is up nearly 11% on the Q'; the stock rose 9.2% after hours.
findings.why_not_priced: SPWH is a $1.31 stock; nothing cross-reads a sub-$100m retailer's department comps into a firearms manufacturer's print 48 hours later, and no SWBI preview I could find mentions it. If it had been read across, SWBI would not have fallen roughly 6% on 2026-09-02/03 into the event (baseline spot $12.305 against the $13.15 quoted in the 2026-09-02 StockStory preview). It is the only true point-of-sale read on SWBI's exact quarter published after every other datum.
findings.independence: Different source, same direction: the call transcript with the verbatim '+8% firearms / +11% ammo' quote and the after-hours reaction (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-sportsmans-warehouse-tops-q2-2026-estimates-shares-jump-93CH-4884682). This is the same company as the press release, so treat release and transcript as one cluster; it is independent of the NICS and Ruger clusters.

findings.finding: Ruger's 8-K for the coincident Apr-Jun 2026 quarter reports net sales $158.1m, +19% y/y, sell-through +19% against adjusted NICS +5%, and distributors' inventories down 45,800 units y/y - the channel manufacturers ship into is lean, which is the condition under which factory shipments run ahead of retail demand rather than behind it.
findings.why_not_priced: Ruger's print is five weeks old and was read as a Ruger new-product story, not as a channel-inventory statement about the industry. The specific unpriced piece is the destocking being finished: SWBI's own Q1 FY26 call had CFO McPherson flagging distributor inventory down over 10% sequentially, and a channel that has now destocked for two years cannot absorb a further leg down, which is precisely the bear case embedded in a 26% drawdown from the 52-week high. If the market had internalised a lean channel it would not be paying only 13.2% for a straddle on a name whose last three prints gapped +17.1%, +18.7% and +23.0%.
findings.independence: SWBI's Q1 FY26 release, quoting the CFO on distributor unit inventory down over 10% sequentially and over 13% y/y (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092796/000119312525196031/d24388dex991.htm). Independent of the NICS cluster and of SPWH.

findings.finding: I can find no company-specific cause for the 16.4% 20-day de-rating: SWBI's only SEC filings since the 17-Jun print are a 7.01 investor-day deck (2026-07-15) and the routine FY26 annual report to shareholders (2026-08-06, a PDF-only submission), with zero Form 4s between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-03 and no 8-K under items 1.01, 2.03, 5.02 or 8.01.
findings.why_not_priced: This is absence used as evidence and I am sizing it small for that reason. But the composition matters: a 26% drawdown with no filing, no insider sale, no downgrade and only two covering analysts is the signature of an unwatched microcap drifting, not of informed selling. If informed money were positioning for a bad print the 25-delta skew would be positive; it is -0.67, i.e. calls are marginally bid, and the put/call open interest ratio is 0.70 on total open interest of just 5,452 contracts with a 36%-of-mid ATM spread. There is no options-market statement here to be on the wrong side of.
findings.independence: none - this rests on one EDGAR query and on the baseline's own skew and open-interest figures, which I cannot revise. I searched for a downgrade, recall, layoff, litigation or offering and found nothing dated August 2026.

searched_and_found_nothing: A cause for the ~6% drop on the morning of 2026-09-03 (baseline spot $12.305 vs $13.15 quoted in the 2026-09-02 StockStory preview) - no news, filing or sector event found
Any SWBI recall, class action, layoff, credit-facility amendment or equity/convertible offering dated August 2026
August 2026 NSSF-adjusted NICS - not yet published by NSSF or Outdoor Wire as of 2026-09-03, so no read on the Q2 FY27 guide the company will give tonight
Any published Q1 FY2027 quarterly revenue or EPS consensus - stockanalysis.com carries FY totals only, from two analysts; the Nasdaq calendar carries no estimate count
SWBI job postings as a signal - roughly 23-24 openings in Maryville TN across Indeed/Glassdoor/ZipRecruiter, but with no historical baseline the level is uninterpretable
SWBI consumer rebate or promotion programme during May-July 2026 (smith-wesson.com/promotions returns 404); a channel-clearing rebate would have been the cleanest negative tell
GunBroker / Gun Genius best-seller rankings - only annual and single-month retail lists, nothing quarter-aligned or share-weighted
Sportsman's Warehouse quarter-to-date August firearms commentary - management's 'we've already started to see it in August' referred to camping and apparel, not firearms
American Outdoor Brands as a cross-read - it reports the identical May-July quarter but not until after today's close, so it is simultaneous rather than a lead

Two search results that looked like current evidence and were not, and are excluded: the SGB 'adjusted NICS +4.0% in July' article is dated 2024-08-06 (and is the source the sweep row cites for July 2026), the SGB 'Firearms Sales Help Sportsman's Warehouse Gain Share In Q2' article is dated 2018-08-23, and Yahoo's 'Why Smith & Wesson Shares Are Plunging' is dated 2024-12-06
baseline_tension: My findings cut against the run-up and sit slightly with the skew: the tape has marked SWBI down 16.4% in 20 days and 26.2% off its high into a print whose industry backdrop measurably improved after the guide was set, while the -0.67 25-delta skew and 0.70 put/call open interest say the options market has taken no directional view at all, so the de-rating is a price move without a corresponding options-market or coverage footprint - and the honest counterweight is that I could not source a cause for it, which is exactly the shape a real unsourced negative would also take.
